correctness.rationale: Exact focal-pool replacement coupling proves formula (1). A second Bernoulli label-switch coupling plus two binomial ratios proves equation (2) including zero-support cases; all factors but MZ−N(k+1) are nonnegative. This establishes the mode(s), H*>1, critical benefit thresholds, and the sign-sequence classification without unproved limits. Independent direct hypergeometric payoff sums and exact rational checks independently verify key identities.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Bernstein variation-diminishing results handle selection gradients averaged using independent co-player probabilities. The present theorem concerns fixed-size finite composition and no-replacement hypergeometric distributions. A general sign-count statement does not determine the exact mode MZ/N−1 or sharp finite benefit multiplier.

originality.rationale: The original finite N-person stag-hunt paper derives the model and hypergeometric payoff sums but describes finite-cooperator phase patterns numerically. Inspection of its extended treatment did not locate the exact mode k=ceil(MZ/N-1) (or its integer tie), the adjacent-difference factorization or the resulting exact benefit boundaries. General infinite-population Bernstein results are conceptually close but do not imply the finite hypergeometric integer formula. Exact-originality certainty is limited by incomplete access to some historical theoretical literature.

value.rationale: A fully specified, finite-population version of a widely studied collective-action dilemma lacked a simple analytical answer in the inspected motivating treatment. The formula locates the greatest selective incentive exactly, identifies an integer divisibility-induced tie and provides sharp benefit-dependent existence and sign-transition phases; these are structurally informative for threshold cooperation and not a generic renaming of an existing table.
